newsitem.title: GERMANY: Lufthansa says fails to reach 1996 savings goal.
newsitem.headline: Lufthansa says fails to reach 1996 savings goal.

text.p: German airline Lufthansa AG said on Monday that it failed by about 300 million marks to achieve its goal of lowering operating costs in 1996.
The airline said in its weekly employee newspaper that the cost-savings programme was affected by higher energy costs and additional spending for electronic data transfer efforts.

Peter Jansen, leader of the airline's "Programme 15" to cut operating costs by 1.5 billion marks by 1999, said the goal of 17.2 pfennigs per offered seat kilometre was missed by 0.5 pfennigs for the year.
But Jansen said more than 850 million marks of the cost-savings goal has so far been secured.

He said in particular that the most savings were seen in procurement, where savings in the hundreds of millions of marks have so far been achieved. The elimination of 900 positions at Lufthansa, which employs more than 58,000 workers, would also lead to triple-digit savings in the millions of marks.

Lufthansa set the goal of cutting 1.5 billion marks in operating costs in a bid to improve profitablity and prepare for full deregulation of the European airline industry, which takes effect on April 1.

Lufthansa on Sunday had said its group net profit in 1996 was lower than the previous year's result of 1.47 billion marks despite solid gains in the number of passengers carried to the Asia, Africa and the Middle East.

Lufthansa managing board member Hemjoe Klein told a news conference at the ITB world tourism trade fair in Berlin that Lufthansa group carried 1.7 percent more passengers in 1996 to a total of 41.4 million.
But Klein said the number of passengers in the parent company fell 0.6 percent to 31.8 million.
